results.1-1: Atropus, the World Born Dead, is a malevolent entity the size of a planetoid that drifts ever closer to the world.
results.2-2: Dendar, the Night Serpent, is a colossal beast that feeds on nightmares generated by its warped mind.
results.3-3: Tharizdun, the Chained God, is a dark spiral of roiling nothingness. It seeks freedom from its millennia-long imprisonment and the extinction of all life.
results.4-4: Xhalovix is an amalgamation of 9,999 mutated planets preparing to ascend to godhood once it has transformed its ten-thousandth world.
results.5-5: Trapped beneath a ruined city, Zargon the Returner seeks loyal worshippers to restore his mutation-steeped realm of slime and decadence. The dark sky reveals his malign will to those who know how to interpret it.
results.6-6: Ejected from the Negative Plane, a nameless evil entity drives mortals to despair by twisting reality into impossible forms.

results.1-1: Apprentice. A Humanoid apprentice relays messages to the characters. The apprentice might be harried, exceedingly proud, or exhausted and overworked.
results.2-2: Magic Mouth. The archmage sends messages through the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplMagicMouth]{Magic Mouth} spell, casting it on objects that vanish once the message is delivered.
results.3-3: Magical Servant. The contact is a loyal servant creature. It might be a Beast or Plant awakened through the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplAwaken0000]{Awaken} spell or a fantastical creature such as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmBlinkDog000000]{Blink Dog} , a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmCouatl00000000]{Couatl} , or a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmFlumph00000000]{Flumph} .
results.4-4: Projected Illusion. The archmage communicates with the characters through the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplProjectIma]{Project Image} spell. The characters might never see the archmage in person.
results.5-5: Sentient Magic Item. A sentient weapon, helmet, or other magic item communicates with the characters on the archmage’s behalf. The item is hundreds of years old and exasperated with the characters’ mistakes, though it loves its archmage creator.
results.6-6: Simulacrum. The archmage uses the Simulacrum spell to create simulacra that issue instructions on the archmage’s behalf.

results.1-1: Aspiring Tyrant. Secretly aspiring to immense political power, the archmage sends the characters on missions that covertly support the archmage’s goal.
results.2-2: Disguised Sage. The archmage disguises themself as a humble apprentice of limited magical ability, while their loud and boastful student pretends to be the archmage. The two keep their true identities secret from the party.
results.3-3: Distracted Genius. The archmage lives in a secluded cottage in the middle of the forest and spends most of their time talking to animals and plants. They employ the characters to handle problems so the mage can spend more time on their harmless personal pursuits.
results.4-4: Forlorn Lover. Having lost the love of their life through hubris to rejection or death, the archmage is focused on winning that individual back or resurrecting them. They need the characters to take care of other problems in the meanwhile.
results.5-5: Redeemed Demonologist. Once a devotee of a demon prince or archdevil, the archmage has renounced evil. They want the characters to solve the problems created when the archmage abandoned their former patron while the archmage focuses on larger challenges.
results.6-6: Wizened Elf. The elf archmage is thousands of years old, their long life magically extended. The archmage remembers errors made over the centuries by well-meaning individuals and employs the characters to stop similar mistakes from happening again.

results.1-1: An empty perfume bottle that smells faintly of longing
results.2-2: Three love letters in the same handwriting, signed with different names
results.3-3: A silk scarf with several hidden pockets
results.4-4: The signature page from a contract
results.5-5: A drinking glass carved with a comet
results.6-6: A gaudy engagement ring with a fake gem

results.1-1: A razor-sharp, violet-tinted talon
results.2-2: An uneven spyglass lens that casts flickering pale-green light
results.3-3: A stone carved with stars in an unfamiliar constellation
results.4-4: Fragments of a prophecy about flumphs
results.5-5: A fern frond that twitches like a tentacle
results.6-6: A small box containing a worm that won’t die

results.1-1: A tin of grave dirt
results.2-2: A self-sterilizing trephine
results.3-3: A chapbook with illustrations of graveyards
results.4-4: A zombie’s twitching toe
results.5-5: A small wreath of dried flowers in an old box
results.6-6: A mysterious organ in a jar of amber fluid

results.1-1: A piece of metal pierced by a tornado-driven twig
results.2-2: A tattered, salt-stained doll
results.3-3: A chunk of volcanic glass
results.4-4: Broken wind chimes
results.5-5: A seashell blackened by a great fire
results.6-6: Bark seared with lightning-shaped lines

results.1-1: Cobra, so it has a flared neck and scaly skin.
results.2-2: Fox, giving it reddish fur and vulpine features.
results.3-3: Panther, so it has sharp claws and a high-pitched scream.
results.4-4: Rabbit, giving it long ears and a skittish demeanor.
results.5-5: Turtle, giving it a blunt snout and shell-like carapace.
results.6-6: Wolf, so it emits eerie howls.

results.1-1: Administrative Assistant. This polished professional has served the institution for decades, seems to know everything, and brooks no arguments.
results.2-2: Anonymous Mail. The characters get their missions via couriers sent by the institution. The group patron might be a single individual pretending to speak for the entire institution.
results.3-3: Mascot. A highly intelligent creature beloved by the staff bonds with the party and serves as an adviser and guide.
results.4-4: New Hire. Newly hired, the contact is inexperienced and can’t answer the party’s questions without consulting their superiors, but they’re well meaning and sincere.
results.5-5: Overeager Graduate Student. This idealistic, advanced student idolizes the party and supports their every action.
results.6-6: Senior Faculty Member. The most famous member of the institution personally delivers all missions and takes great interest in the party’s activities.

results.1-1: Apocalyptic Cult. This cult collects powerful magic lore and items to prepare for a world-ending battle the institution’s leaders know is coming. These leaders don’t tell the characters the full context of their plans, but they need the characters’ help in preparing for the fight.
results.2-2: Magical Warehouse. This institution is dedicated to finding and hiding dangerous magic. It maintains a warehouse filled with anonymous crates, each containing a powerful magic item or tome of magical lore. The institution needs the characters to track down and recover dangerous items to store in the warehouse, which itself might be magical.
results.3-3: Military School. At this institution, mages train to serve in the realm’s armed forces as officers and mobile artillery units. The institution emphasizes obedience, duty, and patriotism, and it needs disciplined characters to perform missions to ensure its longevity.
results.4-4: Religious Order. A religious order devoted to one or more gods of magic teaches spellcasting, performs religious rituals for the community, and pursues the gods’ goals. The institution needs the characters to further these goals.
results.5-5: Underground Society. This informal network of aristocrats, mages, and scholars meets in inns, taverns, and other social venues to pursue clandestine schemes that might include sabotage, thievery, and mayhem. The institution needs discreet characters to perform delicate tasks.
results.6-6: University. Students from all over the world come to this famous university to study magic. The institution needs the characters to perform missions to preserve and further its reputation.

results.1-1: A compass that spins lazily
results.2-2: A map of a lost valley
results.3-3: A chip of ice that never melts
results.4-4: A ring inscribed “bring me home again”
results.5-5: Wicker from the basket of a hot air balloon
results.6-6: Four orange leaves with unfamiliar shapes

1-1.name: All-Seeing
1-1.description: While attuned to this item, you have &Reference[Truesight] with a range of 30 feet.

2-2.name: Empowering
2-2.description: While attuned to this item, one of your ability scores (DM’s choice) increases by 2, to a maximum of 24.

3-3.name: Gravitational
3-3.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplReverseGra]{Reverse Gravity} (save DC 18) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

4-4.name: Heliacal
4-4.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplSunburst00]{Sunburst} (save DC 18) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

5-5.name: Prismatic
5-5.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplPrismaticS]{Prismatic Spray} (save DC 18) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

6-6.name: Spellguarding
6-6.description: While holding or wearing this item, you have Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

7-7.name: Stupefying
7-7.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplPowerWordS]{Power Word Stun} (save DC 18) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

8-8.name: Subjugating
8-8.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplDominateMo]{Dominate Monster} (save DC 18) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

9-9.name: Tranquil
9-9.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplMindBlank0]{Mind Blank} (targeting yourself only) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

10-10.name: Vanishing
10-10.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can take a &Reference[Magic] action to give yourself the &Reference[Invisible] condition for 1 hour or until you end it (no action required). Once this property has been used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

results.1-1: Awakened Beasts. One or more awakened Beasts deliver the details of the characters’ missions. The characters might consistently meet with an awakened Beast quest giver, or they might receive each quest from a different creature.
results.2-2: Enigmatic Dreams. The entity communicates with the characters through the Dream spell, sending them strange dreams suggesting specific courses of action.
results.3-3: Lackey. A Commoner servant attends the entity and delivers messages to the characters along with dire warnings of the consequences of failure.
results.4-4: Mirror Reflections. The entity communicates to the characters via mirrors using illusions. The entity appears as the reflection of one of the characters, or the entity’s image replaces that of a character.
results.5-5: Prophecy. The entity communicates indirectly by spreading prophecies to those nearby. The characters are expected to undertake missions that would fulfill the prophecies.
results.6-6: Shape-Shifter. The entity never openly appears to the characters, but creatures that claim to be the entity’s servants deliver the characters’ assignments. These creatures are the entity in disguise, using the Shapechange spell or a similar ability.

results.1-1: Angel. This powerful Celestial from the Upper Planes disguises itself to mingle among ordinary people and seeks virtuous characters to join its fight against evil.
results.2-2: Beast Lord. An immortal, legendary spirit in animal form, such as an @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmAnimalLord0000]{Animal Lord}, protects the environment and its inhabitants. The spirit needs emissaries as well as strike teams to combat threats to the land.
results.3-3: Ancient Dragon. A chromatic dragon who has turned away from evil behavior or a metallic dragon who champions good recruits the characters for their valiant heroics.
results.4-4: Giant. A @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmStormGiant0000]{Storm Giant} leader who lives in a flying castle high above the realm, hidden by clouds or a perpetual storm, has a vested interest in matters on the ground and sponsors the characters to act as the giant’s emissary.
results.5-5: Reformed Rakshasa. A Lawful Good @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmRakshasa000000]{Rakshasa} works layered schemes against other Fiends and recruits the characters to further its mission.
results.6-6: Undying Steward. A powerful mage helped found the realm and is thought long dead, but they have survived as a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.actors.Actor.aunBaelnorn00000]{Baelnorn} or a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.actors.Actor.aunTaisus0000000]{Taisus} (see chapter 6 for both).

results.1-1: A long fake beard
results.2-2: A fancy pen that never runs out of ink
results.3-3: A bag of broken teeth
results.4-4: A scrap of paper with several crossed-out passwords and the word “caiman” circled
results.5-5: Two identical playing cards with unfamiliar suits
results.6-6: A featureless mask with small eyeholes

results.1-1: An undersea volcano near a busy bay is showing signs of an imminent eruption. Crucible Keepers who can operate underwater rush to study it and warn those nearby of its dangers.
results.2-2: Oracles predict a terrible earthquake will devastate a metropolis in the next few weeks. Crucible Keepers race to construct magical pylons to absorb its earth-rending energy.
results.3-3: A gate to the Elemental Plane of Fire is expected to appear in remote farmland. Crucible Keepers hope to stabilize and eventually close the gate—but before closing it, they want to venture through it to study planar conflagrations.
results.4-4: An ancient white dragon that planned to bury a peaceful valley beneath an avalanche has been slain. Crucible Keepers study the weakened snowpack so they can redirect the avalanche away from the nearby villages.

results.1-1: An advertisement for a past circus performance, featuring your likeness
results.2-2: A small tin of white greasepaint
results.3-3: A green wire stem that produces an illusory flower for 1 minute when brandished dramatically
results.4-4: A fine silk ribbon, two inches wide and nine feet long
results.5-5: Bronze finger cymbals
results.6-6: A battered top hat

results.1-1: Several @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmGladiator00000]{Gladiators} fight a beholder, which is an illusion—a hidden @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPerformerLegen]{Performer Legend} uses the Major Image spell to simulate the monster.
results.2-2: Six trained mammoths form a pyramid, and a giant toad hops up to the top; all the animals are realistic illusions.
results.3-3: A @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPerformerMaest]{Performer Maestro} sings an eerie ballad about a shipwreck while @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPerformer00000]{Performers} on trapezes swing over and through the illusion of a grand, doomed galley.
results.4-4: Two @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmSatyr000000000]{Satyrs} play a compelling melody while they lead volunteers from the audience through a cage of glaring lions; the volunteers and lions are illusions.
results.5-5: Two @UUID[Compendium.dnd-dungeon-masters-guide.equipment.Item.dmgDmtKnight0000]{Knights} joust while riding horses cloaked in illusions to look like rhinoceroses.
results.6-6: A @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPerformerMaest]{Performer Maestro} navigates a wondrous illusory forest and grows 50 feet tall to step over the tallest tree at the act’s conclusion.

results.1-1: A gnome named Molly Nettle (Small @UUID[Compendium.dnd-arcana-unleashed.actors.Actor.aunConjurerArchm]{Conjurer Archmage} ; see chapter 6) keeps a gingerbread house in the Feywild where she welcomes Horizon Weavers but shoos away all others. She doesn’t understand why visitors find her residence and her child-shaped cookie sculptures off-putting.
results.2-2: The Tidepool Larder is an air-filled grotto on the Elemental Plane of Water, stocked with salted fish and other seafood. The reclusive @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmMarid000000000]{Marid} caretaker, Baliob, hides from visitors and doesn’t charge for supplies.
results.3-3: A dour @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmGithzeraiPsion]{Githzerai Psion} named Ut maintains a peaceful monastery called Ninebells on a rocky island in Limbo. Ut lets non-Horizon Weavers stay no more than nine hours.
results.4-4: Scuttlebeam is a beached ship in a Feywild forest. Its married keepers, a goliath named Rusty Jenk (Medium @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPirateCaptain0]{Pirate Captain} ) and an orc named Trellie (Medium Mage ), don’t remember how the ship got here.
results.5-5: Falling Up, a floating inn in the Elemental Plane of Air, is managed by three human, semiretired Horizon Weavers (Medium @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmMage0000000000]{Mages} ), all eager to swap tales.
results.6-6: A way station in Bytopia called the Shuttle’s Rest was recently reduced to ruins by an enormous, clawed creature.

results.1-1: Environmentalists . The faction seeks to magically preserve the realm’s natural spaces and wildlife. It doesn’t receive funding and resources from the government, so it recruits the characters to act as its agents.
results.2-2: Magical Intelligence Agency. This government agency, which protects the realm from magical threats, needs the characters to investigate cases and neutralize dangers.
results.3-3: Magical Military. The characters are soldiers in the realm’s army. They’re given orders by individuals of higher rank who expect to be obeyed.
results.4-4: Rebel Faction. The faction opposes the current rulers of the realm and operates from a secret base. The characters are tasked with gathering resources and allies for a coming revolt, though if the characters are caught, the rebels disavow all knowledge of them.
results.5-5: Ruling Party. The faction is in power due to its members’ magical prowess. The faction needs the characters to sniff out threats to ensure the nation’s safety—and the faction’s political supremacy.
results.6-6: Shadow Cabinet. The shadow cabinet operates clandestinely. The characters know the truth and must keep their missions secret lest the rulers discover and disband the faction.

results.1-1: Excitable Artificer. The contact is eager for the characters to test their latest inventions—which are often unsafe.
results.2-2: Harried Bureaucrat. This administrator has a busy schedule and lacks the time or resources to supervise every task. They assign missions in a rush and leave the party to sort out the details.
results.3-3: Naive Intellectual. This reclusive intellectual with encyclopedic knowledge but no field expertise suggests impractical or unrealistic courses of action.
results.4-4: Political Officer. Responsible for prioritizing the faction’s political agenda, the officer frequently questions the characters’ loyalty.
results.5-5: Public Relations Expert. The contact magically manipulates public perception and strives to make the characters popular.
results.6-6: Well-Mannered Aristocrat. This genteel individual personally meets with the characters to give them their missions, usually over tea in their magic-filled abode.

1-1.name: Amicable
1-1.description: When you fail an ability check made to influence a creature while holding or wearing this item, you can roll [[/r 1d6]] and add the number rolled to the check, potentially turning the failure into a success. This property can be used three times, and the item regains expended uses of this property daily at dawn.

2-2.name: Conversational
2-2.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplTongues000]{Tongues} from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

3-3.name: Crusading
3-3.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCrusadersM]{Crusader’s Mantle} from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

4-4.name: Displacing
4-4.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplBlur000000]{Blur} from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

5-5.name: Frightening
5-5.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplFear000000]{Fear} (save DC 15) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

6-6.name: Fulminating
6-6.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplLightningB]{Lightning Bolt} (save DC 15) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

7-7.name: Immolating
7-7.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplFireball00]{Fireball} (save DC 15) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

8-8.name: Quickening
8-8.description: As a Bonus Action while holding or wearing this item, you can infuse yourself with magical velocity for 1 minute or until your Concentration ends. While you are infused, your Speed is doubled, and &Reference[Opportunity Attacks] against you are made with Disadvantage. Once this property has been used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

9-9.name: Restorative
9-9.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can take a &Reference[Magic] action to cast both @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplCureWounds]{Cure Wounds} and @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplLesserRest]{Lesser Restoration} , targeting the same creature. Once this property has been used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

10-10.name: Skulking
10-10.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplPasswithou]{Pass Without Trace} from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

11-11.name: Studious
11-11.description: When you fail an ability check made as part of the &Reference[Study] action while holding or wearing this item, you can roll [[/r 1d6]] and add the number rolled to the check, potentially turning the failure into a success. This property can be used three times, and the item regains expended uses of this property daily at dawn.

12-12.name: Vigilant
12-12.description: While holding or wearing this item, you have Advantage on Initiative rolls and Wisdom (Perception) checks.

Seers of Sea and Sky Trinkets.name: Seers of Sea and Sky Trinkets

results.1-1: A piece of driftwood with natural whorls and gnarls that spell out your name
results.2-2: A windsock
results.3-3: A tide chart for an unfamiliar seashore
results.4-4: A roll of seaweed with cryptic symbols written on it in octopus ink
results.5-5: A small cog from a lighthouse’s turning mechanism
results.6-6: Four oddly shaped white feathers that fit together to form a perfect triangle

results.1-1: A tin of lotion to ease rashes
results.2-2: A religious tract for an unfamiliar deity of healing
results.3-3: A child’s drawing of two parents smiling
results.4-4: A utensil with a fork on one end and spoon on the other
results.5-5: A pouch of sweet spices
results.6-6: A windup toy soldier holding a large shield

results.1-1: Bound by Debt. A creature the trickster saved from a terrible fate brings the characters messages to work off the debt incurred by this rescue.
results.2-2: Bound Demon. A demon the trickster bound long ago is magically prevented from doing evil and satisfies itself with pranking the party and encouraging them to solve problems with violence.
results.3-3: Faerie Dragon. The trickster’s @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmFaerieDragonYo]{Faerie Dragon Youth} attendant occasionally slips away to give advice and gifts to the characters. The trickster might be unaware of the faerie dragon’s mercurial actions.
results.4-4: Minuscule Fey. The contact, a @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmPixie000000000]{Pixie} or @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmSprite00000000]{Sprite} , is desperately in love with the trickster and considers the party to be the means by which the contact can earn the trickster’s affection.
results.5-5: Transformed Enemy. The trickster overcame a hated rival long ago and transformed the rival into a sentient magic item, a talking animal, or another form. Now the rival delivers messages to the party and warns them against the trickster.
results.6-6: Wise Centaur. This wise, patient, and elderly @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmCentaurWarden0]{Centaur Warden} has trained generations of adventurers. The centaur doesn’t always agree with the trickster but respects their power.

results.1-1: Bored Immortal. This being has lived for centuries or perhaps millennia and has seen it all. They desperately crave entertainment and generously pay anyone who provides spectacle—the more dangerous, the better.
results.2-2: Child Prodigy. A young child of incredibly powerful magical beings, the prodigy has inherited great power but doesn’t yet have the maturity to use it wisely. The prodigy uses their force of will and considerable monetary resources to convince the characters to undertake their capricious missions.
results.3-3: God of Mischief. A god devoted to mischief and deception conceals their identity from the party while sending the characters on missions to humiliate the god’s rivals.
results.4-4: Long-Forgotten Archmage. This ancient archmage, long thought dead, possesses great power but is increasingly eccentric and bitter that no one remembers their most glorious past deeds. The archmage hires the characters to fool individuals from the archmage’s past into making amends for perceived misdeeds.
results.5-5: Puckish Fey. This powerful fey serves the archfey ruler of a Domain of Delight as a court jester or is themself an archfey. The fey delights in sending the characters on well-paid missions that further the trickster’s schemes or simply amuse them.
results.6-6: Willful Hag. A hag coven member doesn’t approve of deeds performed by the other hags in the coven and assigns the characters missions to secretly undermine the rival hags.

results.1-1: Imprison those who would oppose him in a vast labyrinth of his own creation called the Maze of Darkness.
results.2-2: Summon a two-headed, Abyssal dragon called the Demodragon (use the @UUID[Compendium.dnd-monster-manual.actors.Actor.mmAdultBlackDrag]{Adult Black Dragon} stat block) and unleash it on a nation.
results.3-3: Recruit heroes to help him thwart the League of Malevolence, a villainous group led by his former lackey, the mage Kelek.
results.4-4: Disguise himself as a wise wizard or noble paladin to trick innocents into giving him a powerful artifact.
results.5-5: Assemble six powerful magic items and use their magic at a site called the Hall of Bones to gain enough power to destroy Tiamat for good.
results.6-6: Find an artifact called the Box of Balefire and keep it away from other villains; Venger fears it could unleash Tharizdun.

1-1.name: Chilling
1-1.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplConeofCold]{Cone of Cold} (save DC 17) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

2-2.name: Deceptive
2-2.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplMislead000]{Mislead} (save DC 17) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

3-3.name: Far-Seeing
3-3.description: While holding or wearing this item, you can cast @UUID[Compendium.dnd-players-handbook.spells.Item.phbsplScrying000]{Scrying} (save DC 17) from it. Once the item has been used to cast this spell, this property can’t be used again until the next dawn.

4-4.name: Fortunate

results.1-1: Council of the Wise. The circle members are the world’s mightiest, most benevolent mages, but the most charismatic of them is secretly a traitor. Most of the characters’ missions are altruistic, but occasionally the traitor sends them on missions meant to sow discord among the group.
results.2-2: Disaster Preventers. The circle members don’t like each other, but they’ve come together to stop the apocalypse. They need the characters to achieve lesser missions while they focus on the larger threat.
results.3-3: Grudging Allies. Longtime enemies, the circle members wreaked great destruction during their conflicts. They’ve agreed to avoid fighting each other, instead using the characters to pursue the goals they can agree on.
results.4-4: Pub Crew. The circle formed as an excuse to drink and socialize. Members have no time for dangerous missions to save the world, sending the characters instead.
results.5-5: War Veterans. The circle members are veterans who have served together in several wars. In their retirement, they prefer to send more energetic operatives—the characters—to stop the next great war.
results.6-6: Well-Meaning Imposters. The circle members are frauds with only minor magical power. They maintain this ruse because without the circle, the realm would collapse into warring factions. If the characters learn of the wizards’ lack of ability, they might continue to work for the circle to avoid larger conflicts.

results.1-1: Abjurer. Specializing in healing and protective magic, the contact wards the characters before adventures, heals them afterward, and urges the characters to be cautious.
results.2-2: Conjurer. The contact specializes in teleportation magic and summoning magical allies. If the party is in great danger, the contact teleports them to safety or sends magical creations to help.
results.3-3: Diviner. Before every mission, the contact delivers enigmatic advice that the characters find useful—if they can decipher its meaning and recall it at the right moment.
results.4-4: Evoker. This evoker proposes the most direct and destructive way to solve any problem. They don’t worry about collateral damage incurred during a mission.
results.5-5: Illusionist. The characters know little about the contact, not even their true appearance or identity. The contact could show up in any context or situation, even appearing to be someone else whom the party knows well.
results.6-6: Necromancer. The contact ghoulishly asks the characters to bring back corpses or body parts from their adventures but is willing to cast the Raise Dead spell if a character perishes on a mission.
